title: Grafana Applies SLOs and Error Budgets to AI Agent Behaviour
gist: Grafana proposes applying SRE tooling (evaluations, SLIs, SLOs and error budgets) to AI agent behaviours such as groundedness, task fulfilment, toxicity and cost, so gradual quality drift becomes measurable even while the agent stays technically up. The article stresses that the SLO is only as good as the underlying evaluators.

insights.claim: Conventional observability shows an agent responded quickly, without errors and with a given token count, but not whether the answer was correct, grounded or useful; Grafana evaluates behaviour itself and turns results into an SLI measured against an SLO.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Observability vendors are extending from system reliability to behavioural reliability, a new product surface.
insights.quote: none necessarily indicate whether its answer was correct, grounded in available information, or useful to the user

insights.claim: Grafana argues against a single 'agent quality score': quality is multidimensional (grounded but expensive, helpful but occasionally toxic, accurate but slow), so behaviours should be measured separately with separate objectives.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Aggregate AI quality scores can hide failures; prefer vendors exposing per-dimension metrics.

insights.claim: Example SLO: 95% of conversations judged fulfilled over 30 days; the remaining 5% is the error budget, the unacceptable behaviour the team explicitly tolerates.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete template for turning AI quality into a governable target.
insights.locator: Once a behaviour can be measured

insights.claim: Error budgets create a decision model: with budget left teams experiment with prompts, models or behaviour; as it is consumed priority shifts to improving quality, mirroring the SRE trade-off between reliability and velocity.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Links AI release pace to measured quality; a governance mechanism for agent deployment.
insights.locator: This approach matters less for the percentage

insights.claim: Agents can keep responding successfully while answers become subtly less useful due to a model change, prompt modification, retrieval change or shifted user behaviour, deteriorating by a fraction of a percentage point per day; error-budget burn makes this drift visible.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Silent degradation is the key agent production risk; burn-rate alerting is the proposed countermeasure.

insights.claim: An agent can be technically available while being operationally unreliable, so the system can remain 'up' while becoming progressively less trustworthy.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Uptime SLAs are insufficient for AI products; behavioural SLAs may become a procurement criterion.
insights.quote: the system can remain "up" while becoming progressively less trustworthy

insights.claim: There is little consensus on acceptable targets (85%, 95% or 99% fulfilment or groundedness), unlike availability targets with decades of experience; Grafana proposes baselining via evaluations and using history to recommend a target, tightening it as the agent matures.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Target-setting practice for AI SLOs is immature, so expect early inconsistency.
insights.locator: The hardest part may not be creating the SLO

insights.claim: An SLO is only as useful as the measurement beneath it: if an LLM judge consistently misclassifies responses the error budget gives false precision, and poor evaluations can reward outputs that satisfy a criterion but not user intent.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Evaluator validation, representative datasets and human review remain necessary costs.
insights.quote: An SLO is only as useful as the measurement underneath it
insights.locator: There is also an important limitation

insights.claim: Evaluations can use an LLM as judge, but deterministic checks such as regular expressions suffice where the behaviour can be identified without an LLM.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Cheaper deterministic evals reduce cost and judge-error exposure.

insights.claim: Grafana's Agent Observability grew out of monitoring its Grafana Assistant, where prompt, model and tool changes made traditional monitoring insufficient; its engineers distinguish offline evaluations from online evaluations on real production interactions.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Vendors dogfooding agents are productizing their own monitoring needs.
insights.locator: Grafana's approach is to establish a baseline

insights.claim: Anthropic uses defined tasks, repeated trials and multiple graders, distinguishing pass@k (succeeds at least once) from pass^k (succeeds consistently across all attempts), the latter being more relevant to production reliability.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Consistency metrics matter more than best-of-k for production agents.
insights.locator: Grafana's SLO approach is part of a broader

insights.claim: OpenTelemetry is working on standardised semantic conventions for agent telemetry; the emerging pattern is evaluations determine correctness, observability provides evidence, and SLOs set the operational threshold.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Standardisation of agent telemetry lowers vendor lock-in in AI observability.
